Messages.Author: legb...@my-dejanews.com
Messages.Body:
We're just back from our easter hols in edinburgh where we played a LOT Of
Sabbat sealed-deck games, which were great fun. And for the first time we
really got to grips with the sabbat withdrawing rules, which are rather good
IMO. In one game i was clinging on with 7 cards in hand and no library,
unable therefore to play any cards or discard without falling into the
withdrawal well. Lady Legbiter's solution was to play Revelations at inferior
and FORCE me to withdraw - a really creative and clever card play, i thought.
Anyway, after a few turns, i actually did manage to withdraw .. once i had
beaten all her vamps into torpor. Did i mention that i got thouroughly beaten
up in most of the games, and that Michael the [10-year old] Childe of
Legbiter built a really SMASHING Tzimisce deck? Well now i did.

I know i keep going on about this but it really is remarkable what a
different game sealed-deck sabbat is. DO try it, if only to prove to your
collective selves that i'm a babbling idiot. i predict you'll have some of
the best fun you've had with your clothes on. Or off, for that matter, if you
play the strip- sabbat variant.

>Lady Legbiter's solution was to play Revelations at inferior

>Anyway, after a few turns, i actually did manage to withdraw

Actually, I believe that with Sabbat Withdrawl Rules, you withdraw
*NOW*. *N* *O* *W*.

I think it's based on the fact that the V:TES rules are about intent to
withdraw, and that the actual withdrawl happens when you succeed in that
(ie your next untap, conditions fulfilled). The actual withdrawl is
that bit of putting your cards away then, not the trying to avoid
combat, blood loss etc. bit.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
legb...@my-dejanews.com wrote:

> James Coupe <ve...@obeah.demon.co.uk> wrote:
> > legb...@my-dejanews.com writes
> > >Lady Legbiter's solution was to play Revelations at inferior

> > >Anyway, after a few turns, i actually did manage to withdraw
> >
> > Actually, I believe that with Sabbat Withdrawl Rules, you withdraw
> > *NOW*. *N* *O* *W*.
> >
> > I think it's based on the fact that the V:TES rules are about intent to
> > withdraw, and that the actual withdrawl happens when you succeed in that
> > (ie your next untap, conditions fulfilled). The actual withdrawl is
> > that bit of putting your cards away then, not the trying to avoid
> > combat, blood loss etc. bit.
>

> Sure, but you have to succeed in your withdrawal. If you get bled or your
> vamps lose blood the withdrawal fails, and you have to try again.

No. As James said, withdrawal is the act of leaving the game. The attempt to
withdraw (Jyhad/V:TES/Revised rules) is just an attempt, it is not "withdrawal"
until the attempt to successful. To succeed in the attempt, you have to avoid
pool/blood loss, combat, etc.

Under the (now obsolete) Sabbat withdrawal rules, you withdraw (leave the
game) automatically when you have too few cards and an empty library during
your untap. You untap your cards and you leave the game. There is no "attempt".

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
Legbiter wrote:
>>If you start a turn without a full hand, and your library is empty, you are
compelled to attempt to withdraw. This means your vampires can take no actions.
If they must hunt, they go to torpor instead. Your withdrawal attempt succeeds
if you lose neither pool nor blood from your vampires between the untap where
you announce your withdrawal attempt, and your next
untap. If withdrawal succeeds, you keep your ante but gain no VP; and your
predator gains no VP for ousting you, either. If it fails, you must try again
on your next turn.>>

I must wonder why you use this rule. Very often in Jyhad, a player runs out of
cards, yet still has a chance of winning. Why compell them to withdraw from the
game when they could just keep playing?

That, and it makes the "I run you out of cards" deck type that much more
inviting to build, and running out of cards was never supposed to be an
automatic loss in Jyhad.

I'm just curious.

Peter D Bakija

Messages.Author: davey sprocket
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 19 Apr 1999, David M. Dávila wrote:

> Really? I built a deck that ABUSES Dirty Little Secrets and it tends to do
> quite a number on its victims library. My version uses Clan Impersonation to
> make the nasty Malks into nastier Nosferatu Antitribu. Each bleed of 6 at +3
> stealth means someone loses 6 cards from their library. Give it a try and
> tell me how successful you are with it. I have just started playing it, and
> it feels fairly effective.

Hmm, I would question the effectiveness of this strategy. If you are
already bleeding for 6 multiple times, your prey should be toast much
sooner than his library. If, on the off chance that your prey survives to
the point where they run out of cards, then I would say the DLS's hurt
them. But in general, decks have more cards than pool, and unless you
combine DLS with some other effect so that you can choose what you burn
(for example, burning all the rush cards, or all the Praxis-type cards)
you wont really be hurting them more than a basic bleed.

-davey!
